designationHistory.name: Tuxedni Reservation
designationHistory.indexText: Theodore Roosevelt signed Executive Order 1039 setting aside the Tuxedni Reservation in Cook Inlet as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds; it is now part of the Alaska Maritime refuge.
designationHistory.note: The 1988 CCP lists Tuxedni Refuge as established February 27, 1909; the order's text and signature date are from the Wikisource transcription. Predecessor unit, not the establishment of Alaska Maritime itself.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge Final Comprehensive Conservation Plan, 1988 (ServCat 105957)
Wikisource transcription of Executive Order 1039 (from a period government printing)

designationHistory.name: Bering Sea Reservation
designationHistory.indexText: Theodore Roosevelt signed Executive Order 1037 setting aside the Bering Sea Reservation as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds; it was later incorporated into the Alaska Maritime refuge.

designationHistory.name: Bogoslof Reservation
designationHistory.indexText: Theodore Roosevelt signed Executive Order 1049 setting aside the Bogoslof islands in the Aleutians as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds; it is now part of the Alaska Maritime refuge.
designationHistory.note: Sources disagree on the day: the 1988 CCP says March 2, 1909; the Wikisource transcription of the order is dated March 3, 1909. Check the original order (National Archives) before publishing a day.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge Final Comprehensive Conservation Plan, 1988 (ServCat 105957)
Wikisource transcription of Executive Order 1049 (from a period government printing)

designationHistory.indexText: Congress created the Alaska Maritime National Wildlife Refuge in the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act, combining eleven existing refuges with about 460,000 acres of additional coastal islands and headlands.

authority.citation: Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act, Public Law 96-487, sec. 303(1)

designationHistory.note: Act approved December 2, 1980 (statute text). Signer is the President in office on that date. Taft-era predecessors (Forrester Island, Hazy Islands, Chamisso, Aleutian Islands) and later ones (Semidi 1932, Simeonof 1958) were not separately verified.
